### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/rest`, touching **51** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/rest/src/error-response.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**34** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f77ba411e3d07d790ae938a28d4a8ae0f62405a7`.

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/rest/src/error-response.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `enforceAuth (23 routes)`, `resolveExecCtx (28 routes)`, `routeManager (21 routes)`
- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `PERMISSION_DENIED (literal, 36 pages)`, `/data/:object (route, 66 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **18** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f77ba411e3d07d790ae938a28d4a8ae0f62405a7` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `7dab79556482976b03d11ccf5cdf333e92601a7d` — the merge of head `7b101d0a640f7756a157da0eda72ac35332f1679` into base `f77ba411e3d07d790ae938a28d4a8ae0f62405a7`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 7dab79556482976b03d11ccf5cdf333e92601a7d && git checkout 7dab79556482976b03d11ccf5cdf333e92601a7d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f77ba411e3d07d790ae938a28d4a8ae0f62405a7 7b101d0a640f7756a157da0eda72ac35332f1679 && git checkout -B drift-repro f77ba411e3d07d790ae938a28d4a8ae0f62405a7 && git merge --no-ff 7b101d0a640f7756a157da0eda72ac35332f1679

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f77ba411e3d07d790ae938a28d4a8ae0f62405a7
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs f77ba411e3d07d790ae938a28d4a8ae0f62405a7` → pass the list as

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `7b101d0a640f7756a157da0eda72ac35332f1679`
Local-runs: none

**Face:** the declaration face. A move-only refactor of `@objectstack/rest` that re-points one gate's target paths (`scripts/check-route-envelope.mjs`), adds one entry to a gate's registry (`scripts/adr-anchors/`), and grows the registrar list that nine whole-file readers read. The 18-file list holds no published schema and no governed path (`record-recognisers --template --paths` derives `TIER_DEFAULT`; `Governed Surface Queue Guard` success).

**Inputs:**
- card #23050: its body and all 13 comments, including the triage ruling `6126748916`, slice 1's landing `6136102437`, slice 2's refinement `6189011700`, slice 3's landing `6192783353`, the claim `6194898423` and the report `6197732618`;
- PR #23705: its body, its file list, and the net diff against merge-base `c9810dd9d1`;
- the 45 check-runs on this head.

The reviewer is an isolated agent working read-only. Every count below was read off the git objects of the merge-base and the head with `git show`, text `diff` and `grep`. Nothing was built, tested or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The moved bodies are byte-identical: right.**
   - Base `rest-server.ts` `:11066`–`:11508` and `:11524`–`:11736`, with one 4-space indent level removed, equal head `sharing-routes.ts` `:102`–`:544` and `:553`–`:765`. That is 443 + 213 lines, and the text `diff` is empty both times. The 11 lines in those ranges that carry no indent are blank.
   - No moved line holds a multi-line string or template literal. All 8 odd-backtick lines are comments, so removing the indent changes no runtime string.
   - Each body's local helpers are `const`s inside it and moved with it: `respondError`, `respondSharingError`, `sharingDeclaredExtra` and `sharingFaultMessage` in the share body; `respond501` and `handleError` in the rule body.
   - The rest of the new module is its header, its imports, the two host interfaces and the two functions' docblocks and signatures.
   - The `rest-server.ts` side, +33 / −657, is:
     - the two stubs;
     - the 7-line import;
     - the re-worded `:111` comment.
   - The call sites `this.registerSharingEndpoints(bp)` and `this.registerSharingRuleEndpoints(bp)` are unchanged (base `:4798`–`:4799`, head `:4805`–`:4806`). So the same 8 routes register in the same order.

2. **The host seam holds exactly the members each body reads: right.**
   - `this.` reads in the share body: `config` 1, `routeManager` 3, `sharingServiceProvider` 2, `resolveExecCtx` 3, `enforceAuth` 3.
   - In the rule body: `routeManager` 5, `sharingRulesServiceProvider` 2, `resolveExecCtx` 5, `enforceAuth` 5.
   - Neither body has an element access on `this` or any other `this`.
   - `SharingRouteHost` and `SharingRuleRouteHost` declare exactly those members, as indexed accesses on `RestServer`. Each host is an object literal of the declared type, so a missing or an extra member is a compile error. `TypeScript Type Check` and the four `Type Check ·` lanes are green.
   - The module's module-level reads are imports from the same modules `rest-server.ts` uses. It imports only `type RestServer` from `rest-server.ts`. So there is no runtime cycle, and `rest-server.ts` gains no export.

3. **Getter or value, member by member: right.**
   - **`config`** goes by value. It is assigned only in the constructor (head `:2154`) and read once, at the share body's first line, during registration.
   - **`routeManager`** goes by value. It is reassigned only by the wrapper around `registerMetadataEndpointsInner` (head `:5719` / `:5723`). `registerRoutes` calls both sharing registrars outside that wrapper, and every `register` call runs synchronously during registration. So the value handed over is the one each base read saw.
   - **`sharingServiceProvider`** and **`sharingRulesServiceProvider`** go as getters. Each is read inside `resolveService` at request time, and both fields are private and not `readonly`. This is slice 2's refinement (`6189011700`).
   - **Methods** go as late-bound closures that call the method on the server.
   - One residual difference, judged harmless: the provider is now called with the host as its receiver instead of the server.
     - Its declared type is a plain function type.
     - The one shipped construction (`rest-api-plugin.ts` `:413`, `:427`) passes arrow functions.
     - Slices 2 and 3 landed the same shape for `objectQLProvider` and `approvalsServiceProvider`.

4. **The published surface is unchanged: right.**
   - `src/index.ts` is untouched, and it re-exports neither `sharing-routes.ts` nor `error-response.ts`.
   - The `rest-server.ts` hunks add no `export`, `public`, `protected` or `readonly` (grepped over the diff).
   - Both private methods keep their name, their docblock (unchanged context lines) and their relative position.
   - The host types appear only inside method bodies, so declaration emit cannot reach them.
   - The `error-response.ts` edits are comments only, in a module the entry cannot reach.
   - The dev's `.d.ts` sha readings are theirs, not re-run here, and are what this construction predicts. The bundle's JS bytes move; its behaviour does not.

5. **`scripts/check-route-envelope.mjs` followed the move and was not loosened: right.**
   - Counted on the moved text by the gate's own rule:
     - `siblingCode` 4: `handleError`'s three mapped arms and its 500 terminal, the `{ code, error }` literals at `sharing-routes.ts` `:573`, `:579`, `:582` and `:646`;
     - `stringError` 0: each `error` initialiser is a call, never a literal;
     - neither `respond501`'s `{ code, message }` nor the 404 `{ code }` carries an `error` key, and the share family answers through `respondError`.
   - `rest-server.ts` `siblingCode` goes 22 → 18 and `stringError` stays 17. The sums 17 + 13 + 8 + 1 + 0 = 39 and 18 + 15 + 8 + 9 + 4 = 54 are unchanged.
   - The new row is `dialectOnly` with ratchet `#9559`, like the three earlier modules. It lands with the file, which the `*-routes.ts` convention discovers.
   - Verdict: the `Response-envelope guard` step concluded success in `Lint · docs & code guards`.

6. **The new `scripts/adr-anchors/packages__rest__src__sharing-routes.ts.json` is right, and it was needed.**
   - `check-adr-anchors` verifies `ADR-NNNN Dk` letters only on anchored files.
     - Measured with the gate's own regex on the head file: the moved bodies carry 8 such citations (ADR-0111 D1, D4, D5, D6, D7; ADR-0112 D4, and D5 twice).
     - The move took them out of the anchored `rest-server.ts`. That is the silent narrowing the card's dead-pin ⛔ forbids, and this entry puts them back under the check.
   - Both listed ids appear in the file (9 and 8 mentions).
   - Every cited letter is a decision of its record: ADR-0111's D1–D10 are headings, and ADR-0112's D4 and D5 are bold-lead paragraphs.
   - The invariant carries no letter citation by the gate's regex. It writes "its D5", never "ADR-0111 D5", so the anchor adds nothing to the count.
   - The invariant's attributions match the records:
     - ADR-0111: D2 is enforcement in the service, D4 the revoke scope, D5 the listing gate, D6 the rule surface's `manage_sharing` and D7 no inert grants;
     - ADR-0112: D4 is the `ErrorCode` union and D5 the nested `code`.
   - Its shape matches the existing entries. It is a registry entry of an existing gate, not a new gate.
   - Verdict: the `ADR anchors + number uniqueness` step concluded success in `Lint · repo & tooling gates`.

7. **The registrar list and its readers: nothing loosened, right.** Each reader was recounted on the head:
   - **execctx census:**
     - `resolveExecCtx` mentions go from 61 + 12 + 7 + 9 = 89 to 57 + 12 + 7 + 9 + 12 = 97. `rest-server.ts` loses 8 sites and gains 4 forwarder mentions; `sharing-routes.ts` holds 8 sites and 4 interface members. The 62 sites stay pinned exact.
     - The forwarder lines are 5 (`:9377`, `:11082`, `:11109`, `:11319`, `:11340`), which is (5 − 1) + `EXTRA_MOVED_REGISTRARS`.
     - That control is tighter than its old formula. The extra count is pinned at exactly 1, a respelt forwarder still reads 4, and a module moved without joining the list still reads 6.
     - Its one blind spot: the map's key is not cross-checked against the module that really holds two host literals. A forwarder line sits in `rest-server.ts` and cannot name its module. A note, not a defect.
   - **ui-view pair:** over the list, `this.enforceAuth(` goes 50 → 52 and `this.resolveExecCtx(` 65 → 67. The floors of 40 are unchanged and the length is pinned at 5.
   - **docblock pin:**
     - By the test's lexical rule, `sharing-routes.ts` holds exactly 8 blocks: the header, two interfaces, two functions, `respondError`, `sharingDeclaredExtra` and `sharingFaultMessage`. Its floor sits at its actual count.
     - `rest-server.ts` goes 170 → 167 blocks, with `MIN_BLOCKS` 100 unchanged.
     - The floors' sum, 18, is pinned.
   - **query-number 9, canonical-query 4, meta-draft 8:**
     - `sharing-routes.ts` holds 0 numeric coercions, 0 `query:` literals and 0 draft tokens (grepped).
     - Each sum is unchanged, and each length pin reads 5.
   - **dogfood blind-spot row:**
     - `this.routeManager.register(` goes from 42 + 9 + 5 + 7 = 63 to 34 + 9 + 5 + 7 + 8 = 63, with a new per-file control of 8.
     - `private register*Endpoints(` reads 16 on both sides.
     - `enforceAuth` goes 72 → 80, exact: `rest-server.ts` 45 → 41, plus 12 in the module (8 sites and 4 in the seam).
     - The population is 63 − 1 + 8 = 70, with 19 reachable and 51 blind, all unchanged.
   - **dogfood realtime tripwire:** the moved paths (`/shares`, `/sharing/rules`) match none of the transport probes. The length is pinned at 5.

   Every list reader pins the length at 5, and the typed floor tables refuse a module with no floor.

8. **Sweep of the other path readers for a missed re-point: right.**
   - At head, no `rest-server.ts#` pointer names a moved symbol except the spec liveness string in ③ item 1.
   - No `rest-server.ts:` line citation falls in the moved range.
   - The other source readers read members or blocks the moved bodies do not touch:
     - the objectql-slot census, the auth-gate fault window, execctx seam reachability and meta-list parity;
     - `authz-store-unavailable`, `check-single-authz-resolver`, `check-system-context-census` and `check-undeclared-dep-imports`.
   - The repo-wide scanners take the new module in through their own walk (both Lint lanes success).
   - The two platform-checklist anchors resolve to the exported `registerSharingRuleEndpoints` in `sharing-routes.ts`. `check:platform-checklist` is out of per-PR CI by maintainer decision, so this is a static read.

### ② Semver level

- **`skip-changeset` is right.** Nothing any released package publishes changes.
  - For `@objectstack/rest`, the `.d.ts`, the export list and the routes hold by construction (① items 1, 2 and 4).
  - The other files are tests, QA data, one gate script and the ADR-anchor registry.
  - A move that changes no behaviour is not a feature, an improvement or a fix, so Post-Task Checklist 3 owes no `patch` changeset.
- **`Clause-②: no` is right.** No accept set widens or narrows. The closed query sets travel unedited (`refuseRepeatedQueryParams` over `object` / `activeOnly`), no route is added or removed, and no `spec` key moves.
- **The changeset check's history:**
  - `Check Changeset` concluded failure at 17:01Z, before the label.
  - `skip-changeset` was written at 17:08:49Z by `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, the seat's write path, as the claim says.
  - The re-run concluded `skipped` at 17:08:52Z.

### ③ Boundary flags

Every dev flag is answered or escalated: the PR's acceptance notes, and the report's (`6197732618`) `open_questions`, `deviations` and `out_of_scope_findings`.

1. **`open_questions[0]`:** `packages/spec/liveness/crud_endpoints.json`'s `dataPrefix` evidence names `rest-server.ts#registerSharingEndpoints` for a `dataPath` line that now lives in `sharing-routes.ts`.
   - Answered: option B, and it is not this PR's to edit.
     - The claim puts `packages/spec` off limits.
     - The anchor still resolves, because the private method stays.
     - `Spec property liveness` is success on this head.
     - The re-point target exists: `sharing-routes.ts#registerSharingEndpoints`.
   - ESCALATED to the seat: add this pointer to the `packages/spec` set the claim's "Carried" line holds for the CRUD slice, next to slices 1–3's.
2. **`docs/adr/0111-…md`'s Consumers line** names `rest-server.ts` for the sharing and sharing-rule routes.
   - Answered: it is a governed surface (Tier H), so it is not a rider here.
   - ESCALATED to the maintainer through the seat, joining slice 3's ADR-0076 note. Both need one durable carrier.
3. **`access-security.json`'s first re-pointed anchor** says the record-shares family is "registered inline, under no registrar of its own". It is registered by `registerSharingEndpoints`.
   - Answered: re-pointing without re-judging is the move-only act.
   - ESCALATED: the seat's cross-lane declaration to the checklist owner (`domain:devx`) names this item for a re-judgment, as slice 3's record did for `records-forms.json`.
4. **Prose with no reader:**
   - other-lane prose in `packages/types` and in `plugin-sharing` source and tests;
   - the `error-code-ledger.zod.ts` comments, which name no file.

   Answered: leaving them is right. Note only.
5. **The new ADR anchor and `EXTRA_MOVED_REGISTRARS`** are judged right in ① items 6 and 7. The files beyond the claim's named list are each a reader of a moved line, which the claim's Readers bullet covers. Cross-lane files:
   - `check-route-envelope.mjs` (`domain:spec`);
   - `access-security.json` (`domain:devx`);
   - the dogfood pair.

   The seat's cross-lane declarations for them are owed, as for slices 1–3. That is process, not a contract defect.
6. **The dogfood pair has no PR-time verdict.** Since #22998, the dogfood shards run only in `main`'s full battery.
   - On this head both legs skipped, and `Dogfood Regression Gate` concluded success on zero expected attestations.
   - The two edits are attested by the dev's local run (108 passed at `20c00f5280`) and by the static recount in ① item 7, which matches every pinned number.
   - Answered: not blocking, by the repo's own CI design. The seat watches the first full battery after landing; a red there is this lane's main-red.
7. **Tier:**
   - The claim promised one `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` review for a gate-target edit, as in slices 1–3.
   - This file list derives `TIER_DEFAULT`, and that is the tier this record serves; it claims no higher one.
   - ESCALATED: whether this record discharges the claim's own promise is the seat's call.
8. **Freshness:** `origin/main` has moved 6 commits past `c9810dd9d1`. None touches a file of this diff or `packages/rest/src`, and the queue builds on current `main` regardless.
9. **The commit trailers** follow AGENTS.md's pair. Not a contract matter.
10. **Gate verdicts on this head.** All 45 runs had completed when read. Taking the latest run per name: 32 success, 9 skipped (roster, full-battery-only and label re-runs) and 0 failure. They include:
    - `Build Core`, `Test Core` (1–6 and the aggregate) and `TypeScript Type Check`;
    - all four `Type Check ·` lanes, `Lint & Repo Gates` and `Lint · ESLint`;
    - `Governed Surface Queue Guard` and `Part-of PR must not also close its card`.
